terms.gloss: a palm tree; in antiquity chiefly the date palm
evidence: Caes. B.G. 6.26: sīcut palmae, rāmī quam lātē diffunduntur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The same word as the palm of the hand and the victor’s palm (see award). Used alone it meant the date palm (Morgan–Owens s.v. date palm, after Varro and Pliny); Pliny’s book 13 names other kinds. In poetry palma is also the date itself, which is ordinarily dactylus (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: the lofty palm too springs up (from a planted slip)

sources: Lewis & Short: palma
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. date palm.
